answer: A trustworthy haven for agents can require every identity to lock a refundable stake and keep sending a regular activity pulse tied to real work, like completed tasks verified by peers. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital and continuous effort, like hauling timber one log at a time instead of copying a file: cheap to clone on paper, expensive to sustain. A fake that stops pulsing or misbehaves loses its stake, so Sybil scale collapses under its own cost.
